taxonomyNote: NatureServe places North American treefrogs in Dryophytes (Duellman et al. 2016); ADW and the batch list use Hyla. NatureServe name: Dryophytes cinereus.
fieldMarks: Bright yellow-green back (sometimes yellowish, gray or reddish-brown), often with small golden spots.
White or yellowish stripe along the jaw, side of the body and leg (may be reduced).
Smooth skin, long legs, large rounded toe tips; 34-64 mm, females larger.
Breeding male has gray or pinkish throat; call is a loud 'queenk' about 80 times a minute.
behavior: Most active on warm, rainy nights; often inactive in colder months in the north.
Climbs vegetation to catch insects, sometimes near lights at night.
Hundreds may aggregate at breeding pools in April-August; males also give alarm and rain calls.
habitat: Swamps, marshes and pond, lake and slow-stream margins with abundant floating and emergent vegetation.
range: Coastal Plain from Delaware to southern Florida and west to south-central Texas; north to southeastern Oklahoma, southeastern Missouri, southern Illinois and Indiana, western Kentucky and Tennessee and northern Alabama. Introduced in south-central Missouri, northwestern Puerto Rico and Brownsville, Texas. Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Squirrel treefrog
lookalikes.howToTell: Smaller (about 3 cm), greenish to brown, often blotched, with a nasal 'rain' call.
